Bioinformatics Portfolio Project

Multi-Omics Integration
in Glioblastoma

MOFA+ latent factor analysis linking DNA methylation, gene expression, and somatic mutations to patient survival in TCGA-GBM

🧬 TCGA-GBM · N=150 ⚙️ mofapy2 0.7.4 📊 lifelines 🐍 Python 3.10 📂 3 Modalities · 5 Latent Factors

Project Overview

Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumour in adults, defined by molecular heterogeneity across three transcriptional subtypes. This project integrates gene expression, DNA methylation, and somatic mutation data using MOFA+ to discover interpretable latent factors and link them to clinical outcomes.

🎯 Objective

Discover shared and modality-specific latent factors driving GBM biology and survival, and benchmark integration strategies for prognostic prediction.

📐 Method

MOFA+ (Bayesian matrix factorisation with ARD sparsity prior) jointly factorises three data matrices, recovering K latent factors with modality-specific weights.

📌 Reference

Data simulated from Verhaak et al. (2010) GBM subtype biology. Survival parameters from published TCGA-GBM clinical outcomes.

GBM Biology & Subtypes

Verhaak et al. (2010) defined three transcriptional subtypes with distinct molecular signatures and outcomes — each with coordinated patterns across genome, epigenome, and transcriptome.

Proneural

Median OS: 19.6 months · N=50
  • IDH1 mutation: 82%
  • ATRX mutation: 72%
  • TP53 mutation: 68%
  • G-CIMP methylation high
  • PDGFRA / OLIG2 overexpression

Classical

Median OS: 13.5 months · N=50
  • EGFR amplification: 88%
  • TERT mutation: 72%
  • CDKN2A deletion: 52%
  • Intermediate methylation
  • NES / SOX2 overexpression

Mesenchymal

Median OS: 6.6 months · N=50
  • NF1 mutation: 42%
  • PTEN mutation: 54%
  • TP53 mutation: 62%
  • Hypomethylated
  • CHI3L1 / MET overexpression

Analysis Pipeline

Five modular Python scripts, runnable end-to-end with python run_pipeline.py.

1
Simulate Multi-Omics Data Generate 150-patient, 3-modality dataset with subtype-specific signal embedded in expression, methylation, and mutations. Survival times drawn from a Weibull model driven by factor scores.
2
MOFA+ Integration Fit mofapy2 model (K=10 init, ARD pruning). Extract factor scores Z (150×5) and per-modality weights W. Export to HDF5 and CSV.
3
Visualise MOFA+ Results Variance explained heatmap, UMAP of factor space, violin distributions, and top-weight lollipop plots (Figs 1–5).
4
Survival Analysis Kaplan-Meier curves by subtype and factor terciles (lifelines). Univariate and multivariate Cox PH regression with forest plot (Figs 6–7).
5
Fusion Strategy Comparison Benchmark early fusion (PCA concat), MOFA+, late fusion (per-view ensemble), and single-view baselines by Harrell's C-index under 5-fold CV (Figs 8–9).

MOFA+ Results

MOFA+ recovered 5 active factors from 10 initialised, with ARD pruning eliminating uninformative components. Total R²: Expression 86.8% · Methylation 81.6% · Mutations 15.3%.

Figure 2. R² per factor per modality. Factor 1 dominates both expression and methylation; Factor 3 is methylation-specific (G-CIMP).
Figure 3. UMAP of 5-factor space coloured by GBM subtype. Clear subtype separation validates factor biological content.
Figure 4. Factor score distributions per subtype. Factor 1 shows the strongest subtype discrimination.
Figure 5. Top-weighted features per factor and modality. Known GBM drivers (EGFR, IDH1, MKI67, MGMT) appear prominently.

Survival Analysis

Factor scores were tested for association with overall survival using Kaplan-Meier estimators (log-rank test) and Cox proportional hazards regression.

Figure 6. Kaplan-Meier curves. Subtype (p=1.7×10⁻¹⁵) and Factor 1 terciles (p=1.7×10⁻⁸) show highly significant separation.
Figure 7. Cox PH forest plot. Factor 1 HR=0.63 (protective) remains significant in multivariate adjustment.

Integration Strategy Comparison

Five integration approaches benchmarked by Harrell's C-index under 5-fold stratified cross-validation.

Figure 8. C-index across strategies. Late fusion and methylation achieve the highest predictive performance; MOFA+ matches expression-only with fewer features.
Figure 9. Modality contribution per MOFA+ factor. Factor 1 is truly multi-modal; Factor 3 is methylation-specific.

Key Findings

5

Active latent factors recovered by MOFA+ from 10 initialised, after ARD sparsity pruning of uninformative components

10⁻¹⁵

Log-rank p-value for subtype survival separation — confirming the biological validity of simulated clinical parameters

0.73

Best C-index (late fusion ensemble) — matching the best single-view baseline while combining information across all three modalities

0.688

MOFA+ C-index achieved with just 5 latent factors — interpretable, compact, and competitive with raw feature baselines

Data Overview

Figure 1. Data distributions across all three modalities. Expression values (log2 TPM), methylation beta values (0–1), and binary somatic mutations — each encoding a different molecular layer of GBM heterogeneity.
